list.name: stage
list.label: Stage
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT type FROM jobs ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Queue depth now
panels.description: PENDING jobs are waiting for a worker slot; PROCESSING are in flight. Both are read live from the jobs table rather than counted out of the log, which is why this stays correct across a backend restart.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT status AS metric, count(*) AS value
FROM jobs
WHERE status IN ('PENDING', 'PROCESSING')
GROUP BY status

panels.title: Pages completed per hour
panels.description: One point per distinct image finishing its QA stage — the closest thing to 'pages through the pipeline'. Counting jobs instead would multiply every page by its six stages.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(updated_at, '1h'), count(DISTINCT image_id) AS "pages"
FROM jobs
WHERE $__timeFilter(updated_at) AND type = 'qa' AND status = 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Stage breakdown — queue wait vs work time
panels.description: started_at is stamped when a worker accepts the job, so wait and work are separable. Rows only carry it from 2026-08-15 onward; anything older shows null work time because the column did not exist when those jobs ran. Before it, the only available number was total = updated_at - created_at, which is why panel-detection used to look like a 184-second stage when most of that was queueing.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  type AS stage,
  count(*) AS runs,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'FAILED') AS failed,
  percentile_cont(0.5)  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (started_at - created_at))) AS "wait p50",
  percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (started_at - created_at))) AS "wait p95",
  percentile_cont(0.5)  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (updated_at - started_at))) AS "work p50",
  percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (updated_at - started_at))) AS "work p95",
  percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (updated_at - created_at))) AS "total p95"
FROM jobs
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND type IN ($stage)
GROUP BY type
ORDER BY "total p95" DESC NULLS LAST

panels.title: Stage work time p95
panels.description: Worker-held time only, excluding queue wait. Flat here with a rising 'total' on the table above means the queue is backing up, not that a stage got slower.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '1h'), type AS metric,
  percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (updated_at - started_at))) AS "p95"
FROM jobs
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND started_at IS NOT NULL AND type IN ($stage)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Recent failures
panels.description: The error column verbatim. trace_id is the same id the backend and worker logs print (first 8 characters) — copy it and grep both containers to get the full story behind a row.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT updated_at AS "when", type AS stage, attempt, left(trace_id, 8) AS trace, image_id, left(error, 200) AS error
FROM jobs
WHERE $__timeFilter(updated_at) AND status = 'FAILED'
ORDER BY updated_at DESC
LIMIT 100

SELECT coalesce(sum(estimated_cost), 0) AS "spend"
FROM job_costs
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '1d'), model AS metric, sum(estimated_cost) AS "cost"
FROM job_costs
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Cost and tokens by model
panels.description: Cost per page is the number to compare across models — total spend just tracks how much was run through each.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  provider,
  model,
  count(*) AS calls,
  count(DISTINCT image_id) AS pages,
  sum(estimated_cost) AS spend,
  sum(estimated_cost) / NULLIF(count(DISTINCT image_id), 0) AS "cost per page",
  sum(prompt_tokens) AS "tokens in",
  sum(completion_tokens) AS "tokens out"
FROM job_costs
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY provider, model
ORDER BY spend DESC NULLS LAST
